title: A Journey through States of Water
seo_title: A Journey through States of Water Class 6 Science Worksheet (NCERT Curiosity Ch 8)
standard_code: Class 6, Curiosity Chapter 8: A Journey through States of Water
standard_text: Three states of water; melting, freezing, evaporation, condensation and boiling; factors affecting evaporation; cooling by evaporation; the water cycle (summary of NCERT Curiosity Chapter 8).
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 6 Science worksheets for NCERT Curiosity Chapter 8: ice, water and water vapour, melting, freezing, evaporation, condensation, what speeds up evaporation, and the water cycle. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Water can be solid, liquid or gas.
key_sub: Heat, wind and a large surface speed up evaporation.
body_html:
How to think about it

Water exists as ice (solid), water (liquid) and water vapour (gas). Ice melts into water at 0 °C, and water freezes at 0 °C. Water changes into vapour by evaporation at any temperature, and quickly by boiling at 100 °C. Vapour cools and changes back to water by condensation, as on a cold glass.

Evaporation is faster when it is hotter, windier and drier, and when the surface is larger. Evaporation cools things, which is why water in a matka stays cool. Evaporation, condensation and rain together make the water cycle.

Example

Drops form outside a cold glass. Why?

water vapour in the air cools

Answer: condensation

Example

Clothes dry faster on a windy day. Why?

wind carries vapour away

Answer: faster evaporation

Common mistakes

  • Thinking drops on a cold glass come through the glass.
  • Thinking evaporation happens only at 100 °C.
  • Calling the white mist from a kettle water vapour.
